extracted.intended_audience: manufacturers, private labelers, distributors, retailers, CPSC staff, and legal counsel involved in section 6(b) disclosures
extracted.subtask_description: Federal Register proposed rule (Supplemental NPR) describing proposed revisions to 16 CFR part 1101 — the CPSC's regulation implementing section 6(b) of the Consumer Product Safety Act governing public disclosure, notice-and-comment, accuracy/fairness steps, exceptions, retraction, and delegation. It guides agency decisionmakers and affected firms on when and how disclosure may occur and what procedures apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory scope / applicability (the Acts)
rubrics_metrics.description: These rules apply to the public disclosure of any information obtained under the Consumer Product Safety Act, the Flammable Fabrics Act, the Poison Prevention Packaging Act of 1970, and the Federal Hazardous Substances Act (collectively, 'the Acts'), or to be disclosed to the public in connection therewith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed edits align the regulation's scope language with section 6(b)(1) and 6(d)(1) of the CPSA; removes references to other laws not specified in the statute. Use the defined term 'the Acts' throughout the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notice and opportunity to comment (section 6(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to public disclosure of information obtained under the Acts, the Commission, to the extent practicable, must provide manufacturers or private labelers with advance notice and a reasonable opportunity to submit comments if the manner in which the consumer product is to be designated or described in the information will permit the public to ascertain readily the identity of the manufacturer or private labeler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default advance-notice period is 15 calendar days (CPSIA amendment). Notices should provide a meaningful opportunity to comment. The rule aligns the regulation's terminology to 'comment' (not 'analysis') to mirror the statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing — calendar days; shortened notice where public health requires
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing references in the regulation specify 'calendar' days; the default notice period is 15 calendar days. The Commission may find the public health and safety requires less than 15 calendar days' advance notice in appropriate circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule explicitly inserts 'calendar' before 'days' for clarity and proposes procedures (§1101.23) for providing less-than-15-day notice when the Commission finds public health/safety requires it. There is also a distinct, shorter 5-calendar-day notice reference for intent to disclose information claimed to be inaccurate (see delegation exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity ascertainability criterion (trigger for notice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must provide notice and opportunity to comment only if the manner in which the consumer product is to be designated or described in the information will permit the public to ascertain readily the identity of the manufacturer or private labeler.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation was revised to focus on whether the public can readily ascertain the firm's identity from the description, rather than requiring the information to pertain to a specific product. If there is question whether the public could readily ascertain identity, the Commission will provide advance notice and opportunity to comment (§1101.13).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reports of harm posted to SaferProducts.gov (6A(f)(1) exclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports of harm posted on the publicly available consumer product safety information database (SaferProducts.gov) are excluded from the requirements of section 6(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may release or identify information contained in a SaferProducts.gov report without 6(b) notice provided it does not characterize the information or relay new/inferential claims and the use is accurate and not misleading. Example: stating 'SaferProducts.gov received 15 reports of harm involving Manufacturer ABC's lamp' is permissible; issuing a consumer warning based on the report would require 6(b) notice. Reports of harm not published on SaferProducts.gov still trigger 6(b) notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information already publicly available (narrowly defined exception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of section 6(b)(1) do not apply to information that has already been made available to the public through sources other than the Commission, provided the Commission clearly indicates the source of the information and the Commission's use of the information is accurate and not misleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may use publicly available sources (e.g., news articles) without notice if it neither characterizes the information nor conveys new information. The integrity of the source is relevant (e.g., reputable newspaper). The Commission should avoid social-media-style posts implying Commission endorsement or action (example given regarding an alarming social media message about strollers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Information substantially the same as previously disclosed (material-difference test)
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements of section 6(b)(1) do not apply to information, not previously disclosed, that in context does not disclose materially more or materially different information about the consumer product than what the Commission previously disclosed in accordance with the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission adopts a 'material difference' standard rather than the 2014 NPR's broader phrasing; the test depends on context and whether the new disclosure adds materially more/different details than prior disclosures. The regulation references §1101.31(d) for further specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subpart C — Form of notice and opportunity to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule prescribes the form of notice and opportunity to comment the Commission will provide to firms under section 6(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed changes address the content and mechanics of notices (§1101.21), disclosure of a firm's comments (§1101.21(b) cross-references), scope of comments sought (§1101.24), timing and extensions (§1101.22), and methods for electronic notice/communication. Notices must include necessary information to enable an informed response; the regulation clarifies how and when comments may be posted or disclosed by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing: requests for extensions and less-than-15-day disclosures
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures and criteria for requests for time extensions of comment periods (§1101.22) and for providing less-than-15-day notice before disclosure (§1101.23).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supplemental NPR retains 'calendar' for timing and proposes rules for handling extension requests, deletions of obsolete phrasing, and standards for when the Commission may shorten notice periods based on public health and safety. Delegation limitations apply to certain findings about shortened notice (see §1101.71(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Circumstances when Commission does not provide notice and opportunity to comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Circumstances under which the Commission will not provide section 6(b)(1) notice and opportunity to comment are enumerated (statutory exceptions and other categories).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These include statutory exceptions under section 6(b)(4) — imminently hazardous products (section 12 filings), violations of safety rules (6(b)(4)(A)), rulemaking proceedings, adjudicatory proceedings, other administrative or judicial proceedings, information submitted under section 15(b) that falls within statutory exceptions, SaferProducts.gov reports, publicly available information (subject to constraints), and information substantially the same as prior disclosures. Details and scope for each exception are provided in Subpart E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps to assure accuracy (general requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before public disclosure, the Commission shall take reasonable steps to assure that the information it intends to disclose is accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedures are set out in Subpart D (§1101.31-34). The Commission must evaluate the reliability of sources, corroborate information where practicable, and take steps proportionate to the significance/reliability of the information to be disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps to assure fairness in the circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Before public disclosure, the Commission shall take reasonable steps to assure that the disclosure is fair in the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fairness includes considering context, whether the disclosure could mislead, and whether necessary qualifications or caveats should accompany the disclosure. The Commission must avoid disclosure that, though factually accurate, would be misleading without context or qualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps to assure disclosure is reasonably related to effectuating statutory purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Before public disclosure, the Commission shall take reasonable steps to assure that the disclosure is reasonably related to effectuating the purposes of the Acts it administers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission should ensure disclosures serve consumer protection or statutory objectives rather than gratuitous release; the decision should weigh the public benefit of disclosure against potential harms to firms and ensure a reasonable relationship to statutory purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retraction requirement and procedure (section 6(b)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission finds it has made a public disclosure of inaccurate or misleading information that reflects adversely upon the safety of any consumer product or the practices of a covered firm, it shall take reasonable steps to publish a retraction of such inaccurate or misleading information in a manner equivalent to the original disclosure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any covered firm may request a retraction; a request must be in writing and include identity, reproduction of the disclosure if practicable, statement of specific inaccuracies, reasons, requested action for retraction, and any supporting data. The Commission will act expeditiously — generally within 30 working days unless good cause exists — and will notify the requester of its decision and reasons. If equivalent publication is impracticable or risks further disclosure, the Commission will take alternative appropriate action consistent with §6(b)(7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for a request for retraction
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for retraction must include: requester identity and relationship, identification of the disclosed information (date, manner, who disclosed it, type of document), statement of specific aspects believed inaccurate or misleading, reasons supporting that belief, requested corrective action, and any additional supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests sent via email or first class mail to the Office of the Secretary; reproduction of the disclosure (image/audio/video/copy) should accompany the request if practicable. The Commission will inform the requester of its decision and reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 15(b) information — protections and disclosure criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Information identified as submitted pursuant to section 15(b) of the CPSA is subject to additional limitations under section 6(b)(5). The Commission generally shall not disclose such information to the public except under specified circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may disclose section 15(b) information if: (i) it has issued a complaint under section 15(c) or (d) alleging the product presents a substantial product hazard; (ii) it has accepted a remedial settlement agreement (e.g., corrective action plan or consent order); or (iii) it publishes a finding that public health and safety requires public disclosure with a lesser period of notice than section 6(b)(1) requires. The Commission may also disclose upon the submitter's consent. Section 6(b)(5) also excludes from application information independently developed by the Commission or information already publicly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and treatment of 'information submitted pursuant to section 15(b)'
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(5) applies to: (1) information provided to the Commission by a manufacturer, distributor, or retailer identified as submitted pursuant to section 15(b) and 16 CFR 1115.13; (2) portions of Commission-generated documents that contain/summarize such information; and (3) oral communications by Commission personnel that reveal or refer to such information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 6(b)(5) does not apply to information the Commission independently obtains, develops, or that is already publicly available (including company press statements, manuals, SEC filings, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Imminent hazard exception (section 12 filings) (§1101.42)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the Commission has filed an action under section 12 of the CPSA (relating to imminently hazardous products), the requirements of section 6(b)(1)-(3) do not apply to public disclosure of information concerning or relating to the consumer product alleged to be imminently hazardous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exception applies once the relevant action is filed in a U.S. district court; information may be disclosed without following section 6(b)(1)-(3) where disclosure is reasonably related to the violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking, adjudicatory, and other proceeding exceptions (§1101.44-46)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 6(b)(4)(B) excepts information 'in the course of or concerning' rulemaking proceedings, adjudicatory proceedings (commencing upon issuance of a complaint), and other administrative or judicial proceedings from the section 6(b)(1)-(3) requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking exception applies upon publication of an advance notice of proposed rulemaking or a notice of proposed rulemaking in the Federal Register; adjudicatory exception applies after Commission files a complaint under specified statutory provisions; 'in the course of' can include information generated earlier but presented in the proceeding; 'concerning' can apply indefinitely after the proceeding starts. Examples include Commissioners' written opinions or public statements about votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of firm's comments and treatment of privileged/work-product material
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation addresses whether and how the Commission may disclose comments submitted by firms, and how to treat materials claimed as attorney work-product or subject to attorney-client privilege.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Supplemental NPR proposes revisions and cross-references (§1101.21, §1101.24, §1101.31, §1101.33) to clarify when firms' comments may be disclosed and how privileged/work-product claims will be handled; commenters raised concerns that disclosure of firm comments could chill cooperation. The Commission will consider privilege and work-product protections when deciding disclosure, subject to statutory constraints and the Commission's duty to assure accuracy and fairness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic notice and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The regulation modernizes the methods for providing notice and receiving comments to reflect advances in information technology, including electronic notice and communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed edits remove outdated language and add provisions for electronic notices and comment submission. The Supplemental NPR incorporates commenters' input and proposes conforming changes throughout §§1101.21, 1101.22, 1101.23, and 1101.25 to permit and clarify electronic methods, while preserving required content and protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority to the General Counsel (§1101.71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission delegates to the General Counsel authority to render all decisions under this part concerning the disclosure of information subject to section 6(b) in many circumstances, subject to enumerated exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegated authority includes decisions when manufacturers provided 6(b) comment and when they failed to furnish comment or consented to disclosure. Findings not delegated to the General Counsel include: (1) findings that public health and safety requires less than 15 calendar days' advance notice of proposed disclosures (§1101.23(b)); (2) findings that public health and safety requires less than 5 calendar days' advance notice of intent to disclose information claimed to be inaccurate (§1101.25(b)); and (3) decisions whether to publish a retraction under §1101.52. General Counsel decisions on delegated matters are not appealable as of right to the Commission but may be referred to the Commission at the General Counsel's discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and criteria for identifying information that does not require 6(b) notice because it was already published by the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission proposes criteria for when new information does not trigger section 6(b)(1) because it is not materially different from information the Commission previously disclosed in accordance with the law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The adopted test focuses on whether the new disclosure, in context, would disclose materially more or materially different information about the consumer product than prior Commission disclosures, with reference to §1101.31(d) for specification. This reduces uncertainty compared to the 2014 NPR formulation.
